chunks: when you stand up for the service of prayer wash your faces and hands up to elbows, and also wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles.
If you are in a state of seminal pollution, then bathe and purify yourself well.

But in case you are ill or are travelling, or you have satisfied the call of nature, or have slept with a woman, and you cannot find water, then take wholesome dust and pass it over your face and your hands,
for God does not wish to impose any hardship on you. He wishes to purify you, and grace you with His favours in full so that you may be grateful.
ai.seo_question: What are the steps for ritual ablution (wudu) and dry ablution (tayammum) in Islam?
ai.summary: Known as the 'Verse of Wudu' (Ayat al-Wudu), this verse is the primary scriptural basis for the four obligatory acts of ablution in Shia jurisprudence, specifically establishing the wiping of the head (masah) and feet (rajul) rather than their washing. It highlights the theological principle of *takhfif* (ease), demonstrating that Allah intends purification without burden, a concept further elaborated in Shia hadith regarding the conditions of water availability and the specific sequence of these ritual acts.
